BillionToOne.why: its revenue comes from selling its own QCT single-molecule NGS prenatal (UNITY) and oncology (Northstar) cell-free DNA tests, processed with proprietary algorithms and run with AI across operations; Q2 2026 revenue grew 64% and oncology revenue 176%, so the stock benefits directly as these precision-medicine tests are adopted and reimbursed
BillionToOne.evidence: BillionToOne Q2 FY2026 call (08-05-2026): CEO - 'our patented QCT, quantitative counting template technology ... achieves single-molecule level precision with next-generation sequencing. This has allowed us to build unique, category-defining products in both prenatal and oncology'; CFO - Q2 total revenue $109 million, up 64%

players.product: QCT single-molecule NGS (smNGS) prenatal (UNITY) and oncology (Northstar) cell-free DNA tests with proprietary algorithms

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 total revenue was $109 million versus $66.6 million a year earlier, up 64%, driven by tests delivered up 35% and ASP up 21% to $551 per test. Prenatal revenue (clinical testing plus clinical trial support and other services) rose 56% to $95.8 million; oncology revenue grew 176% to $13.7 million, an annualized run rate of approximately $55 million. Total test volume was approximately 196 thousand tests, up approximately 8 thousand sequentially. True-up revenue was $2.8 million versus $9.2 million in Q1 2026 and $2.1 million a year earlier; excluding true-up, total revenue grew 8% sequentially. CEO: the annualized revenue run rate has risen from approximately zero to $438 million in six years.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $109 million (+64%); prenatal $95.8 million (+56%); oncology $13.7 million (+176%); ~196 thousand tests (+35%); ASP $551 (+21%); run rate $438 million

quarterly_data.signal: Gross profit was $77.1 million versus $43.5 million, a gross margin of 70.5% versus 65.3% a year earlier, mainly from higher overall ASP. Operating expenses rose 59% to $71.6 million (R&D $17.3 million vs $11.8 million; SG&A $54.3 million vs $33.3 million). Operating income was $5.5 million, a 5% operating margin versus 16% in Q1 2026 and an operating loss of $1.6 million a year earlier; the CFO said slightly over half of the drop from Q1 came from lower true-up revenue and the rest from commercial and R&D investment and faster oncology growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 15%; net income available to common shareholders was $8.1 million, or $0.15 per diluted share. Cash flow from operations was $9.1 million, capital expenditures $4 million and free cash flow $5.1 million; cash and equivalents ended the quarter at $549 million.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 70.5%; operating income $5.5 million (5%); adjusted EBITDA margin 15%; free cash flow $5.1 million; cash $549 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO reiterated the 2026 total revenue outlook of $450 million to $465 million, growth of approximately 48% to 52% over full-year 2025, and said the company expects to keep generating profitability similar to current levels even with significant continued investment; the guidance includes no incremental true-ups beyond those already reported. During the quarter, by mutual agreement, more than $10 million of claims were held while national payers implement BillionToOne's codes in-network; management expects them to resolve through the second half. CEO: there is meaningful upside if these claims are processed and paid, but the company is cautious on timing and magnitude, so guidance is maintained. Management expects gross margin at or above 70% in the long term, with product economics designed to reach 70% to 80% with scale and coverage; an unexpected oncology acceleration could temporarily push it below 70%.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue $450 million to $465 million (~48% to 52% growth); more than $10 million of held claims; long-term gross margin at or above 70%

quarterly_data.signal: Excluding true-ups, ASP rose $15 quarter over quarter, driven by a record number of payer contracts signed in the quarter; reported ASP fell about $20 sequentially only because true-up was $49 per test in Q1 versus $14 per test in Q2. Oncology ASPs were unchanged quarter over quarter pending MolDX coverage for Northstar Response, so all sequential oncology growth came from test volume. CEO: BillionToOne bills the vast majority of its tests under its own PLA codes (its carrier-screening PLA code took effect January 2025) rather than bundled or stacked billing, and is not seeing the carrier-screening payer friction a competitor reported. Management expects overall COGS per test to rise gradually over time as oncology grows faster than prenatal.
quarterly_data.figure: ASP excluding true-up +$15 quarter over quarter; true-up $14 per test in Q2 vs $49 in Q1

quarterly_data.signal: Prenatal products: UnityConfirm, launched May 28 and described by the company as the first and only noninvasive confirmation assay for high-risk pregnancies (it captures and sequences intact circulating fetal cells for 100% fetal fraction), is already ordered by providers for more than 50% of their eligible high-risk Unity aneuploidy patients and is opening 'no-see' health systems; BillionToOne is enrolling what it believes is the largest prospective circulating fetal cell-based study ever conducted. On August 17 the company expands its fetal risk screen to 130 genes, which it calls by far the largest panel on the market that does not rely on partner testing; approximately 50% of providers prefer large panels. CEO: the 130-gene panel should not change reimbursement or COGS economics much but will open health systems that prefer a large panel, and UnityConfirm is a long-term rather than short-term growth driver because health systems need integrations such as EMR before switching labs.
quarterly_data.figure: UnityConfirm ordered for more than 50% of eligible high-risk patients; 130-gene fetal risk screen

quarterly_data.signal: Oncology catalysts: MolDX Medicare coverage for Northstar Response in the immunotherapy (IO) and IO-combination settings is still expected by the end of this year; Response accounts for almost two-thirds of oncology test volume. A June 24 peer-reviewed study in the Journal of Liquid Biopsy (142 patients, more than 570 samples, two prospective cohorts, 12 tumor types) found molecular progression a stronger predictor of worse survival than imaging alone and was designed to support that coverage. The highly sensitive tumor-naive MRD test remains on track to launch by the end of the year. CEO: MRD will launch around the time Response coverage comes in and its volume will not be throttled, so rapid oncology growth can be dilutive to gross margin in the short term.
quarterly_data.figure: MolDX coverage for Northstar Response and tumor-naive MRD launch both expected by year-end; Response almost two-thirds of oncology volume

quarterly_data.signal: On September 1 BillionToOne updates Northstar Select: the panel expands to 102 genes to cover recent and upcoming FDA therapy approvals, including highly sensitive detection of MTAP copy number loss (present in approximately 15% of all cancer patients), and it launches Northstar Origin, a tissue-of-origin add-on that uses QCT-based molecular counting of methylation to deliver 91% top-3 and 86% top-1 accuracy. Roughly 3% of patients present with cancer of unknown primary, and up to 10% in community oncology settings have uncertain diagnoses. CEO: Origin should not change product economics much but should drive incremental adoption; the company's liquid biopsy assays have a QC failure rate below 1% versus 15% to 30% for assays that require tissue sequencing.
quarterly_data.figure: Northstar Select 102 genes; Northstar Origin 91% top-3 / 86% top-1 accuracy; QC failure rate below 1%

quarterly_data.signal: Commercial: BillionToOne added approximately 70 sales representatives in the first half of 2026, ahead of plan, which had some impact on short-term sales productivity; management expects faster growth exiting the year and into early next year as they become fully productive. It launched on the Epic Aura platform in under five months and completed its first Aura health system integration in two weeks from start to first test order; health systems often slot integrations two to four quarters out, and a single health system often represents approximately 1,000 to 3,000 tests per quarter. Volume growth was in line with expectations in prenatal and above expectations in oncology. CEO: expects continued sequential oncology growth, with the cadence varying on calendar effects and health-system onboarding; there is a small, real Q2 seasonality effect that the company does not model.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 70 sales representatives added in H1 2026; approximately 1,000 to 3,000 tests per quarter per health system

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: because oncology tests are scaling quickly, BillionToOne signed the lease for a dedicated 62,000-square-foot oncology production lab directly across from its existing prenatal production lab in Union City, California. Design and build-out are underway, production is expected by the end of 2027, and the facility is designed to support oncology capacity of approximately 5,000 tests per day over time.
quarterly_data.figure: 62,000-square-foot oncology lab; approximately 5,000 tests per day; production expected by end of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: BillionToOne's patented QCT (quantitative counting template) technology achieves single-molecule precision with next-generation sequencing; he believes prenatal and oncology cell-free DNA testing can exceed an estimated $100 billion in the United States alone and that the company is perhaps at less than 1% of what is possible. Its gross margin combined with fiscal discipline and efficient operations incorporating AI produced GAAP profitability at a much lower scale than public competitors, with an accumulated deficit approximately 10% of theirs; the long-term goal is to become a member of the S&P 500.
quarterly_data.figure: estimated $100 billion US prenatal and oncology cfDNA testing opportunity; accumulated deficit approximately 10% of public competitors'
